definition: A technique that combines multiple sets of model weights (such as checkpoints from different training stages or different fine-tuning runs) by averaging them into a single model.
details: Weight averaging techniques, such as Stochastic Weight Averaging, can improve generalization or combine capabilities from multiple related model checkpoints without additional gradient-based training.

explainer.lead: Combines multiple sets of model weights, such as checkpoints from different training stages or fine-tuning runs, by averaging them into one model. It can improve generalization or combine capabilities without additional gradient-based training.

tiers.eli5: Like blending several slightly different soup batches into one pot to get a steadier, more balanced flavor.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers average checkpoints, for example via Stochastic Weight Averaging, to improve generalization or merge related fine-tunes. A pitfall is averaging weights from models that diverged too far, which can degrade performance.
tiers.paperLevel: Given weight sets, the combined model uses their average; Stochastic Weight Averaging averages checkpoints along the training trajectory to improve generalization, and works best when the averaged weights are compatible.

explainer.example: Checkpoints from the last several training epochs are averaged into a single model that generalizes better than the final checkpoint alone.
